title_jp: {戻って|もどって}きた{財布|さいふ}
context: Thursday 17 December: アルちゃん lost his wallet on the {商店街|しょうてんがい} in the morning, and found it already handed in at the {交番|こうばん}: the man from the rice shop had picked it up. In the afternoon he and ハナおばあちゃん share their opinions on why things come back in this town.
scene: Thursday. This morning your wallet vanished on the {商店街|しょうてんがい}. Now ハナおばあちゃん is under the kotatsu, and you tell each other what you think.

phrases.jp: {日本|にほん}は、{財布|さいふ|wallet|4}が{戻って|もどって}くるくらい{安全|あんぜん|safe|4}だと{思う|おもう}。
phrases.en: I think Japan is so safe that wallets come back.

phrases.jp: それは{場所|ばしょ}に{よる||to depend on|4}んじゃないかな。
phrases.en: Doesn't that depend on the place?
phrases.note: 〜による = it depends on. んじゃないかな softens a different opinion.

phrases.jp: {財布|さいふ|wallet|4}の{落とし物|おとしもの|lost item|3}は{届いて|とどいて}いませんか。
phrases.en: Has a wallet been handed in?
phrases.note: The question to ask at a {交番|こうばん} or a station office.

phrases.jp: {5000円|ごせんえん}くらい{入って|はいって}いました。
phrases.en: There was about 5,000 yen in it.
phrases.note: Number + くらい = about. They'll ask what was inside.

phrases.jp: そうかなあ。{僕|ぼく}はちょっと{違う|ちがう}と{思う|おもう}。
phrases.en: Hmm, I'm not sure. I see it a bit differently.
phrases.note: A gentle way to disagree. ちょっと keeps it soft.

dialogue_setting: Thursday afternoon at the {田中|たなか} house. ハナおばあちゃん has come round; you both tell the story of the morning.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: {今朝|けさ}、{商店街|しょうてんがい|shopping street|3}で{財布|さいふ|wallet|4}を{落とした|おとした}。{泣きたい|なきたい}くらい{焦った|あせった|to panic|4}。
dialogue.en: This morning I dropped my wallet on the shopping street. I panicked so much I wanted to cry.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: {駅前|えきまえ}の{交番|こうばん|police box|3}に{行ったら|いったら}、もう{届いて|とどいて}いた。{米屋|こめや|rice shop|2}さんが{拾って|ひろって|to pick up|4}くれたんだ。
dialogue.en: When I went to the police box by the station, it was already there. The man from the rice shop had picked it up.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: {中身|なかみ|contents|3}も{全部|ぜんぶ}そのまま。{信じられない|しんじられない|to believe|3}くらいだよ。
dialogue.en: Everything inside was still there. It's almost unbelievable.

dialogue.speaker: ハナおばあちゃん
dialogue.jp: {驚く|おどろく|to be surprised|3}ことはないよ。{昔|むかし}から、{落とした|おとした}もんはちゃーんと{戻って|もどって|to come back|4}くる{町|まち}{じゃ||(old/regional) = だ|2}よ。
dialogue.en: Nothing to be surprised about. This has always been a town where lost things come back.
dialogue.note: もん = もの; じゃ = だ (old/regional).

dialogue.speaker: ハナおばあちゃん
dialogue.jp: みんな{顔|かお}を{知っとる|しっとる|(regional) = 知っている|2}から{のう||(old) sentence ending = ね|1}。{悪い|わるい}ことなんて、{できん|できん|(regional) = できない|2}くらい{じゃ||(old/regional) = だ|2}。
dialogue.en: Everyone knows everyone's face, you see. You couldn't do anything bad even if you tried.
dialogue.note: 知っとる = 知っている; できん = できない; のう = ね (old).

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: {田舎|いなか|countryside|3}だからってだけじゃないと{思う|おもう}。{拾った|ひろった|to pick up|4}{人|ひと}が{届ける|とどける|to hand in|3}のが{当たり前|あたりまえ|normal, only natural|4}なんだ。
dialogue.en: I don't think it's only because it's the countryside. Handing in what you find is just normal here.

listening.intro: This morning at the {交番|こうばん}, the officer asked you something first. Type what he said.

lines.jp: {財布|さいふ|wallet|4}の{色|いろ}と、{中身|なかみ|contents|3}を{教えて|おしえて}ください。
lines.en: Please tell me the colour of the wallet and what was in it.

grammar.form: amount: number + くらい・ぐらい (10{分|ぷん}くらい, 5000{円|えん}ぐらい) · degree: plain form + くらい ({泣|な}きたいくらい, {信|しん}じられないくらい) · small thing: noun + くらい (これくらい, {電話|でんわ}くらい)
grammar.explanation: With numbers, くらい/ぐらい means 'about'. After a verb or adjective it shows degree: 'so much that…'. It's close to ほど but more casual, and it can also make something sound small: これくらい = 'something this small'. ほど can't do that.

examples.jp: {交番|こうばん|police box|3}まで、{歩いて|あるいて}{10分|じゅっぷん}ぐらいです。
examples.en: It's about ten minutes on foot to the police box.

examples.jp: {声|こえ}が{出ない|でない}くらい{寒かった|さむかった}。
examples.en: It was so cold I couldn't get a word out.

examples.jp: これくらい、{自分|じぶん}でできるよ。
examples.en: I can do something this small myself.

quiz.question: {駅|えき}まで{歩いて|あるいて}{5分|ごふん}＿＿です。
quiz.en: It's about five minutes' walk to the station.

quiz_more.question: {財布|さいふ|wallet|4}がなくて、{泣きたい|なきたい}＿＿だった。
quiz_more.en: My wallet was gone and I felt like crying.
quiz_more.explain: Plain form + くらい: so bad I wanted to cry.

quiz_more.question: これ＿＿、{自分|じぶん}でやるよ。
quiz_more.en: I'll do something this small myself.
quiz_more.explain: Only くらい makes something sound small; ほど can't.

kanji.where: Above the door of the little police box in front of {鷹ノ原駅|たかのはらえき}, next to the word KOBAN.
kanji.breakdown: 交 take turns + 番 turn, watch → officers taking turns keeping watch: a police box.
kanji.related: {警察|けいさつ} = the police. People call the officers お{巡|まわ}りさん.

tip.title: Found it? Hand it in
tip.body: In Japan you take what you find to a {交番|こうばん}. By law the owner can be asked to give the finder 5–20% of its value as thanks, and if no owner turns up in three months, the finder can keep it. Many people simply refuse the reward.

challenge.prompt: ハナおばあちゃん: 「{財布|さいふ}、{戻って|もどって}よかったねえ。この{町|まち}、どう{思う|おもう}？」 Tell her you think this town is so safe that wallets come back. One part is wrong.

parts.jp: {財布|さいふ}が{戻って|もどって}くるだくらい
parts.why: くらい follows the plain verb directly: {戻|もど}ってくるくらい, no だ.

parts.jp: {安全|あんぜん}だと{思います|おもいます}。

challenge.model_answer: この{町|まち}は、{財布|さいふ|wallet|4}が{戻って|もどって}くるくらい{安全|あんぜん|safe|4}だと{思います|おもいます}。
challenge.explanation: {財布|さいふ}が{戻|もど}ってくるくらい describes how safe: 'safe to the point that wallets come back'. くらい goes straight after the plain verb. 〜だと{思|おも}います gives your opinion politely, right for an older neighbour.
challenge.hint: plain verb + くらい, no だ

vocab.note: {財布|さいふ}を{落|お}とす = to drop your wallet.
{米|こめ} rice + {屋|や} shop. Shopkeepers are called 〜{屋|や}さん.
The opposite of {捨|す}てる (throw away).
{信|しん}じられない! = unbelievable! Very common reaction.
{戻|もど}ってくる = come back here. Things and people both.
You {届|とど}ける it; it {届|とど}く (arrives).
{当|あ}たり{前|まえ}じゃん! = obviously! (casual).
{落|お}とす drop + {物|もの} thing. {忘|わす}れ{物|もの} = something left behind.
Always 〜による / 〜によって. {人|ひと}による = depends on the person.

kanji_study.parts: 扌 hand radical + 合 fit together → a hand gathering things off the ground: pick up.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 給 (supply): 給 has 糸 thread on the left, 拾 has 扌 hand.

kanji_study.parts: A picture of a rice plant: a cross for the stalk with grains scattered all around it.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 来 (come): 来 has an extra bar on top.

extras.title: At the police box
extras.intro: What you'll say and hear when something goes missing.

items.jp: {財布|さいふ|wallet|4}を{落として|おとして}しまったんですが…
どこで{落とした|おとした}か、{覚えて|おぼえて}いますか。
items.en: Do you remember where you dropped it?

items.jp: こちらに{名前|なまえ}と{連絡先|れんらくさき|contact details|3}をお{願い|ねがい}します。
items.en: Please write your name and contact details here.

extras.title: Soft ways to disagree
extras.title_jp: やわらかく{反対|はんたい}する
extras.intro: Japanese rarely says 'you're wrong'. Try these instead.

items.note: Agree first, then add your view.

items.jp: {人|ひと}によると{思う|おもう}けど。
items.en: I think it depends on the person, though.

items.jp: そういう{考え方|かんがえかた}もあるね。
items.en: That's one way to see it.
items.note: Polite, often means you don't agree.
